title: xor(xor(a, b), b) = a
statement: For every natural a, b: xor(xor(a, b), b) equals a.

formal.statement: ((x0 : AxNat) -> ((x1 : AxNat) -> Eq.{1} AxNat (AxNat.xor (AxNat.xor x0 x1) x1) x0))

evidence.supports: Nat.xor_xor_cancel_right is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with the type recorded in formal.statement.
evidence.checker_command: cargo run -q --release -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example nat_theorem_inventory -- xor_xor_cancel_right 2>/dev/null | grep -Ec '^Nat\.xor_xor_cancel_right[[:space:]]'
evidence.notes: `build_nat_prelude` admits this theorem only through the trusted `Kernel::add_declaration` gate, which re-checks the proof term against the stated type. `nat_theorem_inventory` exits non-zero for a name that does not exist, and `grep -Ec` consumes the pipe so the tested count (expected >= 1) decides the exit status, never `grep -q` under pipefail. Anchored with `[[:space:]]`, never a literal tab. `--release` is mandatory: this tool builds `creal`/`complex`/`cpoint`, which overflow the default debug thread stack.

evidence.supports: At the discriminating concrete pair (a, b) = (3, 5), xor(xor(3, 5), 5) def-eq's to 3 (xor(3,5)=6, xor(6,5)=3), and the theorem's conclusion does NOT def-eq to the negative control 4; and the theorem re-derives against a genuinely free (a, b) pair, not merely a concrete instance.
evidence.notes: Same fixture as F:nat-xor-xor-cancel-left's compute evidence, which also checks this theorem's discriminating pair in the same test function.

notes:
formal.statement is `Kernel::render_lean` of the admitted type, taken verbatim from `nat_theorem_inventory`, not transcribed by hand. `AxNat` is the kernel's CONSTRUCTED inductive `Nat` (the `Ax` is *axeyum*, not *axiomatized*).

No `ml430` fact for this exact statement was found in the ledger; see F:nat-xor-assoc's notes for the full mirror-check reasoning (Lean4 core lemma cited but not defined in `Mathlib/Data/Nat/Bitwise.lean` at the pinned commit `c5ea00351c28e24afc9f0f84379aa41082b1188f`). Fourth (of four) sub-target Mathlib's own `xor_trichotomy` proof composes; `xor_ne_zero_iff` is NOT built by this fact.

Transported from F:nat-xor-xor-cancel-left via `Nat.xor_comm` twice, rather than redoing the per-bit argument: `xor (xor a b) b = xor (xor b a) b` (congruence on `xor_comm a b`) `= xor b (xor b a)` (`xor_comm (xor b a) b`) `= a` (`xor_xor_cancel_left b a`). This is the cheap direction once `xor_xor_cancel_left` exists -- no new per-bit or `Bool`-level machinery was needed. `Nat.xor_comm` (`xor_order.rs`) is an admitted, axiom-free kernel theorem this proof calls, but it has no `F:nat-xor-comm` fact of its own in the ledger yet, so `depends_on` names only F:nat-xor-xor-cancel-left (the validator requires every `depends_on` entry to resolve to an existing fact id).
